diagnostics.message: The Tables and Rules for the Feasts are not in the supplied source text. Lux places the movable feasts by the 1662 rules as editorially encoded; the dates of the holy days agree with the Kalendar of the 1693 printing.

The Kalendar, the Proper Lessons and the Proper Psalms are not in the supplied text of the Baskerville printing. They are taken from the London printing of 1693 (Text Creation Partnership transcription A28758), pending comparison with the Baskerville pages.
Proper Psalms are appointed for Ash Wednesday (Table of Proper Psalms, “cii. cxxx. cxliii.”), so the psalms of the ordinary course are omitted.
The First Lesson is appointed but its text cannot be given: no text of the Scriptures was chosen for this office.
The Second Lesson is appointed but its text cannot be given: no text of the Scriptures was chosen for this office.
The prayers for the King and the Royal Family are given as printed in 1762.

rubric.text: At the beginning of Evening Prayer the Minister ſhall read with a loud voice one or more of theſe Sentences of the Scriptures that follow; and then he ſhall ſay that which is written after the ſaid Sentences.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: WHEN the wicked man turneth away from his wickedneſs that he hath committed, and doeth that which is lawful and right, he ſhall ſave his ſoul alive.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: I acknowledge my tranſgreſſions; and my ſin is ever before me.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: Hide thy face from my ſins, and blot out all mine iniquities.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: The ſacrifices of God are a broken ſpirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not deſpiſe.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: Rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, ſlow to anger, and of great kindneſs, and repenteth him of the evil.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgiveneſs, though we have rebelled against him: neither have we obeyed the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in his laws which he ſet before us.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: O Lord, correct me, but with judgment; not in thine anger, lest thou bring me to nothing.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: Repent ye; for the Kingdom of heaven is at hand.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: I will ariſe and go to my father; and will ſay unto him, Father, I have ſinned against heaven, and before thee, and am no more worthy to be called thy ſon.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: Enter not into judgment with thy ſervant, O Lord; for in thy ſight ſhall no man living be juſtified.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: If we ſay that we have no ſin, we deceive ourſelves, and the truth is not in us: But if we confeſs our ſins, God is faithful and just to forgive us our ſins, and to cleanſe us from all unrighteouſneſs.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: DEARLY beloved brethren, the Scripture moveth us, in ſundry places, to acknowledge and confeſs our manifold ſins and wickedneſs; and that we ſhould not diſſemble nor cloke them before the face of Almighty God our heavenly Father; but confeſs them with an humble, lowly, penitent, and obedient heart; to the end that we may obtain forgiveneſs of the ſame, by his infinite goodneſs and mercy. And although we ought, at all times, humbly to acknowledge our ſins before God; yet ought we most chiefly ſo to do, when we aſſemble and meet together, to render thanks for the great benefits that we have received at his hands, to ſet forth his most worthy praiſe, to hear his most holy Word, and to aſk thoſe things that are requiſite and neceſſary, as well for the body as the ſoul. Wherefore I pray and beſeech you, as many as are here preſent, to accompany me, with a pure heart, and humble voice, unto the throne of the heavenly grace, ſaying after me:

rubric.text: A general Confeſſion to be ſaid of the whole Congregation, after the Minister, all kneeling.

text.speaker: all
text.text: ALMIGHTY and most merciful Father, We have erred and strayed from thy ways like lost ſheep: We have followed too much the devices and deſires of our own hearts: We have offended against thy holy laws: We have left undone thoſe things which we ought to have done; And we have done thoſe things which we ought not to have done; And there is no health in us. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us, miſerable offenders: Spare thou them, O God, which confeſs their fault: Restore thou them that are penitent; According to thy promiſes declared unto mankind in Christ Jeſu our Lord. And grant, O most merciful Father, for his ſake, That we may hereafter live a godly, righteous, and ſober life, To the glory of thy holy Name. Amen.

rubric.text: The Abſolution or Remiſſion of ſins, to be pronounced by the Priest alone, standing; the People still kneeling.

text.speaker: priest
text.text: ALMIGHTY God, the Father of our Lord Jeſus Christ, who deſireth not the death of a ſinner, but rather that he may turn from his wickedneſs and live; and hath given power and commandment, to his Ministers, to declare and pronounce to his people, being penitent, the abſolution and remiſſion of their ſins: He pardoneth and abſolveth all them that truly repent, and unfeignedly believe his holy Goſpel. Wherefore let us beſeech him to grant us true repentance, and his Holy Spirit; that thoſe things may pleaſe him which we do at this preſent, and that the reſt of our life hereafter may be pure and holy; ſo that at the last we may come to his eternal joy; through Jeſus Christ our Lord.

rubric.text: Then, the Minister ſhall kneel, and ſay the Lord’s Prayer with an audible voice: the people alſo kneeling, and repeating it with him, both here, and whereſoever elſe it is uſed in Divine Service.

text.speaker: all
text.text: OUR Father, which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy Name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven: Give us this day our daily bread; And forgive us our treſpaſſes, as we forgive them that treſpaſs againſt us; And lead us not into temptation, But deliver us from evil. For thine is the kingdom, the power, and the glory, forever and ever. Amen.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: O Lord, open thou our lips;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And our mouth ſhall ſhew forth thy praiſe.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: O God, make ſpeed to ſave us.

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: O Lord, make haste to help us.

rubric.text: Here all standing up, the Priest ſhall ſay,

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son: and to the Holy Ghost;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever ſhall be: world without end. Amen.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: Praiſe ye the Lord.

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: The Lord’s Name be praiſed.

rubric.text: Then ſhall be ſaid or ſung the Pſalms in order as they be appointed. Then a Leſſon of the Old Testament, as is appointed; and after that, Magnificat (or the ſong of the Bleſſed Virgin Mary) in Engliſh, as followeth.

heading.text: The Proper Psalms for Ash Wednesday

gloria.first: Glory be to the Father and to the Son
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever ſhall be

verses.first: HEAR my prayer, O Lord
verses.second: and let my crying come unto thee.

verses.first: Hide not thy face from me in the time of my trouble
verses.second: incline thine ear unto me when I call; O hear me, and that right ſoon.

verses.first: For my days are conſumed away like ſmoke
verses.second: and my bones are burnt up as it were a firebrand.

verses.first: My heart is ſmitten down, and withered liked graſs
verses.second: ſo that I forget to eat my bread.

verses.first: For the voice of my groaning
verses.second: my bones will ſcarce cleave to my fleſh.

verses.first: I am become like a pelican in the wilderneſs
verses.second: and like an owl that is in the deſert.

verses.first: I have watched, and am even as it were a ſparrow
verses.second: that ſitteth alone upon the houſe-top.

verses.first: Mine enemies revile me all the day long
verses.second: and they that are mad upon me are ſworn together againſt me.

verses.first: For I have eaten aſhes as it were bread
verses.second: and mingled my drink with weeping.

verses.first: And that becauſe of thine indignation and wrath
verses.second: for thou haſt taken me up, and caſt me down.

verses.first: My days are gone like a ſhadow
verses.second: and I am withered like graſs.

verses.first: But thou, O Lord, ſhalt endure for ever
verses.second: and thy remembrance throughout all generations.

verses.first: Thou ſhalt ariſe, and have mercy upon Sion
verses.second: for it is time that thou have mercy upon her, yea, the time is come.

verses.first: And why? thy ſervants think upon her ſtones
verses.second: and it pitieth them to ſee her in the duſt.

verses.first: The heathen ſhall fear thy Name, O Lord
verses.second: and all the kings of the earth thy Majeſty;

verses.first: When the Lord ſhall build up Sion
verses.second: and when his glory ſhall appear;

verses.first: When he turneth him unto the prayer of the poor deſtitute
verses.second: and deſpiſeth not their deſire.

verses.first: This ſhall be written for thoſe that come after
verses.second: and the people which ſhall be born, ſhall praiſe the Lord.

verses.first: For he hath looked down from his ſanctuary
verses.second: out of the heaven did the Lord behold the earth;

verses.first: That he might hear the mournings of ſuch as are in captivity
verses.second: and deliver the children appointed unto death;

verses.first: That they may declare the Name of the Lord in Sion
verses.second: and his worſhip at Jeruſalem;

verses.first: When the people are gathered together
verses.second: and the kingdoms alſo, to ſerve the Lord.

verses.first: He brought down my ſtrength in my journey
verses.second: and ſhortened my days.

verses.first: But I ſaid, O my God, take me not away in the midſt of mine age
verses.second: as for thy years, they endure throughout all generations.

verses.first: Thou, Lord, in the beginning haſt laid the foundation of the earth
verses.second: and the heavens are the work of thy hands.

verses.first: They ſhall periſh, but thou ſhalt endure
verses.second: they all ſhall wax old as doth a garment;

verses.first: And as a veſture ſhalt thou change them, and they ſhall be changed
verses.second: but thou art the ſame, and thy years ſhall not fail.

verses.first: The children of thy ſervants ſhall continue
verses.second: and their ſeed ſhall ſtand faſt in thy ſight.

gloria.first: Glory be to the Father and to the Son
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever ſhall be

verses.first: OUT of the deep have I called unto thee, O Lord
verses.second: Lord, hear my voice.

verses.first: O let thine ears conſider well
verses.second: the voice of my complaint.

verses.first: If thou, Lord, wilt be extreme to mark what is done amiſs
verses.second: O Lord, who may abide it?

verses.first: For there is mercy with thee
verses.second: therefore ſhalt thou be feared.

verses.first: I look for the Lord; my ſoul doth wait for him
verses.second: in his word is my truſt.

verses.first: My ſoul fleeth unto the Lord
verses.second: before the morning watch, I ſay, before the morning watch.

verses.first: O Iſrael, truſt in the Lord, for with the Lord there is mercy
verses.second: and with him is plenteous redemption.

verses.first: And he ſhall redeem Iſrael
verses.second: from all his ſins.

gloria.first: Glory be to the Father and to the Son
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever ſhall be

verses.first: HEAR my prayer, O Lord, and conſider my deſire
verses.second: hearken unto me for thy truth and righteouſneſs ſake.

verses.first: And enter not into judgment with thy ſervant
verses.second: for in thy ſight ſhall no man living be juſtified.

verses.first: For the enemy hath perſecuted my ſoul; he hath ſmitten my life down to the ground
verses.second: he hath laid me in the darkneſs, as the men that have been long dead.

verses.first: Therefore is my ſpirit vexed within me
verses.second: and my heart within me is deſolate.

verses.first: Yet do I remember the time paſt; I muſe upon all thy works
verses.second: yea, I exerciſe myſelf in the works of thy hands.

verses.first: I ſtretch forth my hands unto thee
verses.second: my ſoul gaſpeth unto thee as a thirſty land.

verses.first: Hear me, O Lord, and that ſoon, for my ſpirit waxeth faint
verses.second: hide not thy face from me, leſt I be like unto them that go down into the pit.

verses.first: O let me hear thy loving-kindneſs betimes in the morning, for in thee is my truſt
verses.second: ſhew thou me the way that I ſhould walk in, for I lift up my ſoul unto thee.

verses.first: Deliver me, O Lord, from mine enemies
verses.second: for I flee unto thee to hide me.

verses.first: Teach me to do a thing that pleaſeth thee, for thou art my God
verses.second: let thy loving Spirit lead me forth into the land of righteouſneſs.

verses.first: Quicken me, O Lord, for thy Name’s ſake
verses.second: and for thy righteouſneſs ſake bring my ſoul out of trouble;

verses.first: And of thy goodneſs ſlay mine enemies
verses.second: and deſtroy all them that vex my ſoul, for I am thy ſervant.

gloria.first: Glory be to the Father and to the Son
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever ſhall be

verses.first: MY ſoul doth magnify the Lord
verses.second: and my ſpirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.

verses.first: For he hath regarded
verses.second: the lowlineſs of his hand-maiden.

verses.first: For, behold, from henceforth
verses.second: all generations ſhall call me bleſſed.

verses.first: For he that is mighty hath magnified me
verses.second: and holy is his name.

verses.first: And his mercy is on them that fear him
verses.second: throughout all generations.

verses.first: He hath ſhowed strength with his arm
verses.second: he hath ſcattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts.

verses.first: He hath put down the mighty from their ſeat
verses.second: and hath exalted the humble and meek.

verses.first: He hath filled the hungry with good things
verses.second: and the rich he hath ſent empty away.

verses.first: He remembering of his mercy hath holpen his ſervant Iſrael
verses.second: as he promiſed to our forefathers, Abraham and his ſeed, for ever.

rubric.text: Or elſe this Pſalm: Except it be on the nineteenth day of the month, when it is read in the ordinary courſe of Pſalms.

gloria.first: Glory be to the Father and to the Son
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever ſhall be

verses.first: O Sing unto the Lord a new ſong
verses.second: for he hath done marvellous things.

verses.first: With his own right hand, and with his holy arm
verses.second: hath he gotten himſelf the victory.

verses.first: The Lord declared his ſalvation
verses.second: his righteouſneſs hath he openly ſhowed in the ſight of the nations.

verses.first: He hath remembered his mercy and truth toward the houſe of Iſrael
verses.second: and all the ends of the world have ſeen the ſalvation of our God.

verses.first: Shew yourſelves joyful unto the Lord, all ye lands
verses.second: ſing, rejoice, and give thanks.

verses.first: Praiſe the Lord upon the harp
verses.second: ſing to the harp with a pſalm of thankſgiving.

verses.first: With trumpets alſo and ſhawms
verses.second: O ſhew yourſelves joyful before the Lord, the King.

verses.first: Let the ſea make a noiſe, and all that therein is
verses.second: the round world, and they that dwell therein.

verses.first: Let the floods clap their hands, and let the hills be joyful together before the Lord
verses.second: for he cometh to judge the earth.

verses.first: With righteouſneſs ſhall he judge the world
verses.second: and the peoples with equity.

rubric.text: Then a Leſſon of the New Testament, as it is appointed. And after that, Nunc dimittis (or the Song of Simeon) in Engliſh, as followeth.

placeholder.label: Galatians 1
placeholder.reason: No text of the Scriptures was chosen.

gloria.first: Glory be to the Father and to the Son
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever ſhall be

verses.first: LORD, now lettest thou thy ſervant depart in peace
verses.second: according to thy Word.

verses.first: For mine eyes have ſeen
verses.second: thy ſalvation,

verses.first: Which thou hast prepared
verses.second: before the face of all peoples;

verses.first: To be a light to lighten the Gentiles
verses.second: and the glory of thy people Iſrael.

rubric.text: Or elſe this Pſalm: Except it be on the twelfth day of the month.

gloria.first: Glory be to the Father and to the Son
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever ſhall be

verses.first: GOD be merciful unto us, and bleſs us
verses.second: and ſhow us the light of his countenance, and be merciful unto us;

verses.first: That thy way may be known upon earth
verses.second: thy ſaving-health among all nations.

verses.first: Let the peoples praiſe thee, O God
verses.second: yea, let all the peoples praiſe thee.

verses.first: O let the nations rejoice and be glad
verses.second: for thou ſhalt judge the folk righteouſly, and govern the nations upon earth.

verses.first: Let the peoples praiſe thee, O God
verses.second: yea, let all the peoples praiſe thee.

verses.first: Then ſhall the earth bring forth her increaſe
verses.second: and God, even our own God, ſhall give us his bleſſing.

verses.first: God ſhall bleſs us
verses.second: and all the ends of the world ſhall fear him.

rubric.text: Then ſhall be ſaid or ſung the Apostles Creed, by the Minister and the people standing.

text.speaker: all
text.text: I Believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth: And in Jeſus Christ his only Son, our Lord; Who was conceived by the Holy Ghost, Born of the Virgin Mary, Suffered under Pontius Pilate, Was crucified, dead, and buried; He deſcended into hell; The third day he roſe again from the dead, He aſcended into heaven, And ſitteth on the right hand of God the Father Almighty; From thence he ſhall come to judge the quick and the dead. I believe in the Holy Ghost; The holy Catholick Church; The Communion of Saints; The Forgiveneſs of ſins; The Reſurrection of the body, And the Life everlasting. Amen.

rubric.text: And after that theſe Prayers following, all devoutly kneeling; the Minister first pronouncing with a loud voice,

lines.speaker: minister
lines.text: The Lord be with you;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And with thy ſpirit.

lines.speaker: minister
lines.text: Let us pray.

rubric.text: Then the Minister, Clerks, and People, ſhall ſay the Lord’s Prayer with a loud voice.

text.speaker: all
text.text: OUR Father, which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy Name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done, in earth as it is in heaven: Give us this day our daily bread; And forgive us our treſpaſſes, as we forgive them that treſpaſs against us; And lead us not into temptation, But deliver us from evil. Amen.

rubric.text: Then the Priest standing up, ſhall ſay,

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: O Lord, ſhow thy mercy upon us;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And grant us thy ſalvation.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: O Lord, ſave the King.

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And mercifully hear us, when we call upon thee.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: Endue thy Ministers with righteouſneſs;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And make thy choſen people joyful.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: O Lord, ſave thy people;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And bleſs thine inheritance.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: Give peace in our time, O Lord;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: Becauſe there is none other that fighteth for us, but only thou, O God.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: O God, make clean our hearts within us;

lines.speaker: people
lines.text: And take not thy Holy Spirit from us.

rubric.text: Then ſhall follow three Collects: The first of the day: The ſecond for Peace: The third for Aid against all Perils, as hereafter followeth: Which two last Collects ſhall be ſaid at Evening Prayer without alteration.

heading.text: The Collect of the Day: Ash Wednesday

text.speaker: minister
text.text: ALMIGHTY and everlaſting God, who hateſt nothing that thou haſt made, and doſt forgive all the ſins of thoſe who are penitent; Create and make in us new and contrite hearts, that we worthily lamenting our ſins, and acknowledging our wretchedneſs, may obtain of thee, the God of all mercy, perfect remiſſion and forgiveneſs; through Jeſus Chriſt our Lord. Amen.

rubric.text: This Collect is to be read every day in Lent after the Collect appointed for the day.

heading.text: The Second Collect at Evening Prayer.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: O God, from whom all holy deſires, all good counſels, and all just works do proceed: Give unto thy ſervants that peace which the world cannot give; that our hearts may be ſet to obey thy commandments, and alſo that by thee we being defended from the fear of our enemies may paſs our time in rest and quietneſs; through the merits of Jeſus Christ our Saviour. Amen.

heading.text: The Third Collect, for Aid against all Perils.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: LIGHTEN our darkneſs, we beſeech thee, O Lord; and by thy great mercy defend us from all perils and dangers of this night, for the love of thy only Son, our Saviour Jeſus Christ. Amen.

rubric.text: In Quires an Places where they ſing, here followeth the Anthem.

heading.text: A Prayer for the King’s Majesty

text.speaker: minister
text.text: O Lord, our heavenly Father, high and mighty, King of kings, Lord of lords, the only Ruler of princes, who dost from thy throne behold all the dwellers upon earth; Most heartily we beſeech thee, with thy favor to behold our moſt gracious Sovereign Lord, King G EOR G E ; and ſo repleniſh him with the grace of thy Holy Spirit, that he may alway incline to thy will, and walk in thy way: Endue him plenteouſly with heavenly gifts; grant him in health and wealth long to live; strengthen him that he may vanquiſh and overcome all his enemies, and finally, after this life he may attain everlasting joy and felicity; through Jeſus Christ our Lord. Amen.

heading.text: A Prayer for the Royal Family

text.speaker: minister
text.text: ALMIGHTY God, the fountain of all goodneſs, we humbly beſeech thee to bleſs our gracious Queen C HAR L OTTE , her Royal Highneſs the Princeſs Dowager of Wales, and all the Royal Family: Endue them with thy Holy Spirit; enrich them with thy heavenly grace; proſper them with all happineſs; and bring them to thine everlaſting kingdom; through Jeſus Christ our Lord. Amen.

heading.text: A Prayer for the Clergy and People.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: ALMIGHTY and everlaſting God, who alone workest great marvels; Send down upon our Biſhops and Curates, and all Congregations committed to their charge, the healthful Spirit of thy grace; and that they may truly pleaſe thee, pour upon them the continual dew of thy bleſſing: Grant this, O Lord, for the honour of our Advocate and Mediator, Jeſus Christ. Amen.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: ALMIGHTY God, who hast given us grace at this time with one accord to make our common ſupplications unto thee; and dost promiſe that when two or three are gathered together in thy Name thou wilt grant their requests; Fulfill now, O Lord, the deſires and petitions of thy ſervants, as may be most expedient for them; granting us in this world knowledge of thy truth, and in the world to come life everlasting. Amen.

text.speaker: minister
text.text: THE grace of our Lord Jeſus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowſhip of the Holy Ghost, be with us all evermore. Amen.

rubric.text: Here endeth the Order of Evening Prayer throughout the Year.
